Atlanta Beltline property rights secured
stories.summary: The Atlanta Beltline can be completed by 2030, according to its CEO. The project has now secured the final section of property rights needed to finish the trail. The timeline is set, pending the actual construction.

stories.title: Environment advocate calls for cooling strategies
stories.summary: Cooling centers and emergency alerts are insufficient for extreme heat, an environment justice advocate writes. Cities should prioritize energy-efficient cooling and housing improvements within their climate strategies. The current approach is described as falling short of the necessary infrastructure.

The debate over wooded buildings
stories.summary: Buildings featuring trees have become a global architectural trend, adopted by studios including BIG and MVRDV. Critics frequently label the structures as greenwashing or gimmicks. The industry remains divided on whether the arboreal additions provide genuine environmental benefits or serve primarily as a visual statement.

stories.title: Peabody delivers 189 Passivhaus homes in Deptford
stories.summary: Peabody and Higgins Partnerships have completed 189 Passivhaus homes at Deptford Landings. The development includes 130 social rent units and 59 shared ownership properties. This marks the housing association's first full Passivhaus project, with residents expected to move in before the end of the year.

stories.title: Hoffmann Green partners with Isometric for cement certification
stories.summary: Hoffmann Green Cement Technologies has partnered with Isometric to certify its clinker-free cements under the Low Carbon Cement Protocol. The company claims this enables the issuance of Environmental Attribute Certificates. It is the first cement manufacturer to market these certificates for its clinker-free products.

stories.title: Lagos school wins global environmental award
stories.summary: Slum2School Green Academy in Epe has won the 2026 World’s Best School Prize for Environmental Action. The academy, which uses bamboo construction, is the first Nigerian institution to receive the award. The prize was presented during a virtual ceremony organized by T4 Education.

stories.title: Cyberabad plans net-zero headquarters
stories.summary: The Cyberabad Municipal Corporation has invited tenders for a 169-crore twin-tower headquarters. The proposed 241,540 square foot complex will be built on the edge of Kotha Kunta lake. The project is officially designated as a net-zero green building.

Prestige University named World Building of the Year
stories.summary: Prestige University in Indore has been named World Building of the Year at the World Architecture Festival. Designed by Sanjay Puri Architects, the structure features stepped courtyards intended to maximize natural ventilation. The design also functions as an open-air amphitheatre for 9,000 students.

stories.title: Gurugram to use parks for flood mitigation
stories.summary: After spending 300 crore on drains that failed to prevent monsoon flooding, Gurugram is shifting its strategy to parks. The government has ordered the development of retention ponds and water bodies across 247 acres of green space. The city will now attempt to store water instead of carrying it away.

stories.title: Neral station receives green building rating
stories.summary: Neral railway station has earned a Gold Rating from the Indian Green Building Council for its recent upgrades. The project included the installation of solar power and water conservation measures. The station serves as a primary transit hub for tourists traveling to Matheran.

stories.title: Indore university building wins global architecture award
stories.summary: The Prestige University building in Indore has been named World Building of the Year 2026 at the World Architecture Festival. The project, designed by Sanjay Puri Architects, features open terraces that accommodate 9,000 students. It outperformed architectural projects from across the globe.

stories.title: Vadnagar museum wins international design award
stories.summary: The Anant Anadi Vadnagar Archaeological Experiential Museum has received Germany’s Red Dot: Best of the Best Award 2026. The museum features a walkway suspended over a 4,000-square-metre excavation site. It is the first museum in India to win the award in the exhibition design category.

stories.title: Barcelona home restoration draws on local history
stories.summary: Architect Raúl Sánchez has restored a two-story home on Calle Aiguafreda, a street once defined by communal laundry wells. The project was commissioned for a family in a neighborhood that has since moved on from its original function as a place to wash clothes.

stories.title: Desai Chia balances privacy and light in Bethesda
stories.summary: Desai Chia Architecture has completed a private home in Bethesda, Maryland, designed to feel open and light-filled on a dense suburban lot. The architects utilized a large light well to bring daylight deep into the interior while addressing the proximity of neighboring houses.

stories.title: David Chipperfield completes pavilion for Anselm Kiefer
stories.summary: David Chipperfield Architects has finished a concrete pavilion in Künzelsau, Germany, dedicated to the work of artist Anselm Kiefer. The building houses a monumental painting reflecting on the Holocaust, establishing what the firm describes as an intimate relationship between art, architecture, and remembrance.

stories.title: Zaha Hadid Architects completes first African project in Rabat
stories.summary: The Théâtre Royal de Rabat has reached completion sixteen years after its initial design. The project, which faced a long delivery timeline and complex engineering, stands as the first completed work in Africa by Zaha Hadid Architects. The venue is part of a wider urban transformation.

stories.title: Estudio MMX completes City of Indigenous Arts in Tepic
stories.summary: Mexican studio Estudio MMX has completed the City of Indigenous Arts in Tepic, a project featuring four brick buildings and public plazas. The development aims to recover a neglected site and give physical form to the multicultural identity of Nayarit through working cultural infrastructure.

stories.title: Tuckey Design Studio renovates Yorkshire home
stories.summary: Tuckey Design Studio has renovated a country house in Yorkshire, using a dark palette of timber and terracotta to evoke the feeling of a wine bar. The project included expanding the early 2000s property and adding a bespoke wine storage cabinet and tasting area.

stories.title: Kanal-Centre Pompidou opens in Brussels
stories.summary: The Kanal-Centre Pompidou opens on November 28th, 2026, within a restored 1930s Citroën garage. Designed by a consortium including EM2N and Sergison Bates, the 40,000-square-meter museum proposes a more open relationship between cultural institutions and the city through extensive free public space.

stories.title: SO to IL proposes glass-scaled museum for Norwegian forest
stories.summary: Architecture studio SO to IL has presented a design for the Kistefos Museum in Jevnaker, Norway. The building features a translucent skin of glass scales intended to mirror the changing colors of the surrounding forest, with an organic silhouette that appears to float above the ground.

stories.title: Studio Gang completes Wisconsin leadership campus
stories.summary: Studio Gang has completed a women’s conference center on a lakeside hill in Wisconsin. Founder Ann Drake stated she wanted to build a space designed with women in mind, as they spend much of their careers in rooms that were not.

stories.title: Research team tests earthen construction with paper waste
stories.summary: A research team has developed a framework for using excavated subsoils and recycled paper by-products in three-dimensional printing. The study tracks material behavior from geotechnical classification through robotic extrusion trials to convert earthen waste into functional building materials for the construction sector.

stories.title: Jindal Steel introduces 1650 mm-wide coated steel
stories.summary: Jindal Steel has launched a 1650 mm-wide coated steel product under its Jindal Panther brand. The company unveiled the material at its Rangotsav event in Bhubaneswar, marking an expansion into high-value downstream building solutions designed for India's evolving construction needs.

stories.title: Flexible thermal insulation market projected to grow
stories.summary: The flexible thermal insulation market reached a valuation of USD 7.13 billion in 2025. Analysts project the market will grow to USD 13.5 billion by 2036, driven by building owners and equipment makers seeking to control condensation and meet energy-efficiency requirements.

stories.title: Green cement market expected to reach $74.4 billion
stories.summary: The global green cement market is projected to grow from US$37.7 billion in 2026 to US$74.4 billion by 2033. Growth is supported by demand for sustainable materials and efforts to reduce carbon emissions from cement manufacturing through alternative binders and industrial byproducts.

stories.title: Bellway completes first Passivhaus project in West Sussex
stories.summary: Bellway has completed eight Passivhaus homes at its Perceval Grange development in Midhurst. While the project was initially driven by local planning requirements, it now serves as a demonstration of how developers might approach the mainstream adoption of ultra-low-energy housing.

stories.title: Senate committee proposes mass timber incentives
stories.summary: The Senate Appropriations Committee has released spending text that could provide federal incentives of up to US$20,000 per housing unit built with mass timber. The proposal directs the Department of Housing and Urban Development to develop and study the initiative from its research budget.

stories.title: Argeli shrub fibers shown to increase mortar strength
stories.summary: A laboratory study found that adding Argeli shrub fibers to cement mortar increased flexural strength by 23.49 percent. The researchers concluded that the fibers, when used at an optimal dosage, also improved compressive and tensile strength compared to plain reference mortar.

stories.title: This 3D-printed ADU is a family labor of love. ‘We’re home’
stories.summary: As he stepped over the threshold of his new home for the first time, John Treherne’s jaw dropped. Surrounded by floor to ceiling windows, new furniture and dozens of friends and family, Treherne stared around in awe, amazed at his new living situation. “I love it,” he said. “This is

stories.title: Velletri museum restores Roman sundial
stories.summary: The Oreste Nardini Civic Archaeological Museum has returned a marble hemicyclium sundial to display following a restoration. The project used 3D printing to reconstruct a missing lion’s paw, adhering to the principle of reversibility so the addition can be removed without damaging the original marble.

stories.title: Architectural identity in flux
stories.summary: Architectural styles are increasingly detached from their origins, with classical columns appearing on self-built homes and modernist compositions on residential façades. These transformations reflect shifting architectural decisions, raising questions about how identity develops when traditional characteristics are applied outside their original context. The meaning remains in the eye.

stories.title: Window performance beyond the frame
stories.summary: Le Corbusier famously described windows as paramount to architecture, yet modern performance depends on more than just the frame. While two windows may share identical dimensions and materials, their effectiveness in regulating light, ventilation, and thermal comfort varies significantly based on glazing, hardware, and installation exposure.

stories.title: Karnataka government studies Japan waste-to-energy model
stories.summary: A delegation led by Chief Minister DK Shivakumar visited Osaka’s Maishima Incineration Plant to evaluate its waste-to-energy technology. The facility, operational since 2001, processes 900 tonnes of municipal waste daily using two incinerators. It generates 32 MW of power, meeting its own needs while supplying surplus electricity to the grid.

stories.title: Karnataka officials visit Japanese incineration plant
stories.summary: Karnataka officials toured the Maishima incineration plant in Osaka to study international waste-to-energy models. The facility processes 900 tonnes of municipal waste daily and generates 32 MW of power, providing electricity to the grid. The visit is part of a broader effort to adopt established infrastructure management practices.

stories.title: IIT Madras to host electric freight dialogue
stories.summary: IIT Madras will host the eCV Dialogue on January 21-22 to address India's electric freight transport transition. With medium and heavy-duty vehicles contributing nearly 25 percent of India's transport emissions, the event aims to bridge the transition gap and establish actionable policies for the country's electric highway.

stories.title: The solitary life of the slender loris
stories.summary: Known as the forest baby, the slender loris is a solitary primate that hunts by night using large eyes to spot insects. Its thin limbs are ill-suited for leaping, requiring a well-connected canopy for movement. It rarely descends to the ground, preferring to communicate through clicks and whistles.

stories.title: Neelakurinji blooms draw crowds to Kerala
stories.summary: Thousands of visitors have flocked to Kerala’s Chokramudi to view Neelakurinji flowers. While the main garden limits daily visitors to 1,000, tourists also access nearby slopes. The plant is protected under the Wildlife Protection Act, yet faces threats from habitat degradation, invasive species, and ongoing tourism-related activities.

stories.title: Call for balance in Chennai urban planning
stories.summary: Dr. Sowmiya Anbumani has urged for a balance between real estate growth and environmental protection. Highlighting the role of wetlands in flood resilience, she raised concerns over shrinking lakes in Tamil Nadu, construction-related emissions, and the growing challenge of managing urban waste in the face of rapid development.

stories.title: Mangaluru satellite study links urban growth to heat
stories.summary: A thirty-year satellite analysis of Mangaluru shows that rapid urban development between 1993 and 2023 has significantly raised land surface temperatures. Researchers established a direct relationship between the conversion of natural landscapes into impervious surfaces and the intensification of localized thermal ecological stress in the coastal city.

stories.title: Media debates COP31 outcome
stories.summary: Following the rejection of the proposed Antalya pact, media outlets are divided over the cause of the COP31 outcome. Some attribute the lack of a final agreement to oil-rich nations, while others point to European reluctance on climate finance. The future of the UN climate process remains under scrutiny.

stories.title: Urban heat islands raise city temperatures
stories.summary: Urban heat islands occur when natural landscapes are replaced by pavement and buildings that retain thermal energy. These metropolitan areas are typically 0.5 to 4 degrees Celsius warmer than surrounding rural communities, even when both locations share the same weather forecast. The city effectively traps the heat.

stories.title: The unglamorous foundation of architecture
stories.summary: Geotechnical investigation is the process of drilling and testing soil to determine what a building site can support. While it is the least glamorous part of a project and often faces client resistance, it remains the deciding factor in whether a structure will stand once built.

stories.title: Greenery as a response to urban heat
stories.summary: Taiwan’s dense concrete structures and basin topography trap heat, driving inner-city temperatures 2 to 4 degrees Celsius above suburban baselines. Multi-tiered greenery is proposed as a solution to support urban biodiversity and mitigate the heat island effect, reducing the reliance on air conditioning and its associated emissions.

stories.title: Horn of Africa cities prepare for El Niño
stories.summary: IGAD and UN-Habitat have released a guide to help Horn of Africa cities transition from reactive disaster response to proactive resilience. The initiative emphasizes cross-border coordination and the use of local knowledge, recognizing that climate risks do not respect national boundaries when extreme rain events occur.

stories.title: Apartment living cited for energy efficiency
stories.summary: Vector expects Auckland’s electricity demand to rise by 16 percent over the next decade. The Green Building Council suggests that apartment living could mitigate this pressure, as smaller units with fewer external walls are more energy-efficient than standalone homes. The grid is waiting for the shift.

stories.title: Canada Bay adds 540 trees to local streets
stories.summary: The City of Canada Bay has planted 540 trees across its suburbs this year, supported by a state grant. Mayor Michael Megna stated that increasing tree canopy is an effective way to reduce urban heat and make public spaces more welcoming, particularly during the warmer months of the year.

stories.title: Design competition launched for Katong pedestrian mall
stories.summary: The Urban Redevelopment Authority and Singapore Institute of Architects have launched a design competition to transform East Coast Road into a pedestrian mall. The project seeks proposals to improve walking connections, add greenery, and celebrate the heritage of the Katong area based on recent community feedback.

stories.title: Singapore seeks designs for Katong pedestrian mall
stories.summary: The Urban Redevelopment Authority has opened a design competition for a new pedestrian mall between i12 Katong and Katong V. Architects are invited to submit proposals that improve cycling and walking connections, provide public amenities, and incorporate greenery while reflecting the character of the historic Katong district.

stories.title: Synaps 2.0: Rethinking Architectural Design with AI
stories.summary: Architecture has always existed between imagination and representation. Long before a building takes physical form, it begins as an idea about space, structure, movement, and human experience. stories.title: Kestrel Labs adds Autodesk Forma integration
stories.summary: Kestrel Labs has updated its building code compliance platform to include integration with Autodesk Forma, browser-based 3D review, and expanded state-code coverage. The company says its AI application has seen nothing but positive momentum since its June 2026 launch. Compliance is now available outside of Revit.

stories.title: Nomic adds automated CAD drafting to AI platform
stories.summary: Nomic has extended its AI-powered drawing review software to include automated CAD drafting. Users can provide natural language descriptions or existing drawings for revision, with the platform returning editable CAD files and plotted PDFs. The company is moving from identifying errors to actively addressing them.

stories.title: Cloud Lab brings AI safety tools to 7,300 Korean sites
stories.summary: In the 1990s, construction sites had a strong culture of putting construction schedules ahead of safety. Cloud Lab CEO Lee Yo-hoon came to recognize the need for safety management after witnessing a fatal worker accident on site. Seeing the victim's young child playing at the funeral, unaware of the father's

stories.title: Saudi AI startup 009 raises $1.4 million
stories.summary: Riyadh-based startup 009 has raised $1.4 million in a pre-seed round led by Outliers Venture Capital. Founded in 2026, the company develops AI agents to automate administrative workflows. Its technology creates digital agent twins to help companies test automation using historical data before deployment.

stories.title: Staff at Edinburgh College of Art oppose course closures
stories.summary: Over 100 staff members at Edinburgh College of Art have signed an open letter criticizing the university's decision to close three craft-focused design courses. The institution will stop admitting students for jewellery, textiles, and performance costume from 2027. The letter expresses deep concern regarding the move.

stories.title: Carlo Ratti appointed director of 2027 Seoul Biennale
stories.summary: The Seoul Metropolitan Government has appointed architect Carlo Ratti as artistic director for the 2027 Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism. Ratti, a professor at MIT, is known for exploring how digital technology and human behavior reshape cities. He previously led the Venice Biennale's architecture exhibition.

stories.title: Carlo Ratti to lead Seoul architecture biennale as artistic director
stories.summary: Italian architect Carlo Ratti will serve as artistic director of the sixth Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism next year. Ratti led the Venice Biennale's International Architecture Exhibition last year. The Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism is an international event held every two years since 2017.
